sample_unit: panoramic radiographs (4500 finding-level decisions per reader)
models_evaluated: three multimodal LLMs accessed via consumer web interfaces (names not given in text)

links.outcome: Diagnostic performance of multimodal LLMs versus expert radiologists on same radiographs against CBCT reference
links.effect: Expert sensitivity 89.5-91.6%, specificity 92.0-93.0%, accuracy 91.8-92.9% versus LLMs 75.1-83.1%, 88.0-90.0%, 86.8-89.0%; reader effect significant (p<0.001).
links.quote: Under the consumer-interface conditions and access period tested, the LLMs performed below the experts, particularly for high-risk findings, and should not be used independently to evaluate panoramic radiographs.

links.outcome: Sensitivity of LLMs for high-risk findings on enriched single-center data
links.effect: In the exploratory high-risk group, expert sensitivity was 90.9-93.2% versus 62.9-78.0% for the LLMs; the dataset was finding-enriched and single-center, so estimates cannot be transferred to routine populations.
links.quote: In the exploratory high-risk group, expert sensitivity ranged from 90.9 to 93.2% versus 62.9-78.0% for the LLMs.

screen.reason: Retrospective reader study evaluating and comparing diagnostic accuracy of multimodal LLMs against human radiologists for incidental findings on dental radiographs without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
